relationship: Supplements completed 89488dd/Q1-Q4 only. Supersedes no pins, answers, checks or target intakes. Q5 follow-duration is already answered by coordinator and is not repeated here.
citation_format: ID:start-end denotes inclusive one-based lines in sources[ID].member; SHA256 hashes exact raw member bytes. Formulas describe static source, not executed behavior.

slot.numbering: slot <n> is zero-based, command range 0..15 inclusive, initial formation_slot=0. It assigns the addressed bot(s) the same requested slot, not successive squad positions. No argument produces usage, not an implicit reassignment.
slot.parsing: SplitArgs collects digit-only uint64 tokens, optionally with g/s/c suffix (multipliers 10000/100/1); other tokens including -1, +1 and decimals are ignored. slot uses the FIRST collected number, narrows it to int, then clamps negative int to0 or int>15 to15. Thus ordinary slot16 ->15; slot-1 alone is usage, not a negative clamp. stoull overflow is dropped. Huge uint64-to-int narrowing and suffix multiplication are not safe evidence that every oversized input clamps to15; native/compiler behavior is untested.
slot.assignment: Sets formation_slot and saves squad state. If owner_command==Follow and owner_target is nonempty, queues BuildFollowIntent immediately, using legacy ComputeFormationOffset; no manual-mode-expiry check occurs in this slot branch. regroup reissues BuildFollowIntent if an owner target exists. Slot assignment neither reorders other bots nor chooses a placement index.
slot.automatic: Ordinary Follow calls AutoAssignFormationSlot then persists. It keeps a unique slot; on collision, picks the first free index0..15 among registered AIs returned by BotsOwnedBy(owner.account_id). If all16 are used, collision remains. Despite its active-Follow comment, this helper does not filter those other AIs by current Follow mode or living state. A manual pin can therefore change on a later Follow collision.
slot.scope: Dispatch resolves one or multiple addressed bots then calls the same authorized single-bot handler; slot is not a group-wide reservation. Active owner-follow geometry independently recomputes rank/GUID indices (G), so slot does not pin that index. Placement likewise ignores formation_slot; its log uses i+1/count, which is a one-based display distinct from slot <n>.

placement.docs: BOT_COMMANDS line125 describes fixed positions, optional selectors, here/target/cursor and return after fights. Add-on lists eight shapes and tight/normal/wide. This is manual world-position placement with Stay, not moving owner-follow Formation or immediate legacy FollowIntent.

gap.limits: Slots clamps a directly supplied numeric gap to1..20 yards, but these commands accept gap words, not arbitrary numeric yards. No owner-formation 0.75 scaling or GUID jitter is applied. Default shape in the add-on is circle; the server rejects a missing/unknown shape, despite its initial local enum being Circle. Gap is not exact pairwise separation for every shape.

placement.frame: n is selected bot count, capped40; n=0 produces no slots. f is forward and l is left; angles radians, all lengths upstream WoW yards. CEN below subtracts each axis bounding-box midpoint, NOT the centroid. ROW(n,w,h,v) emits row=floor(i/w), start=row*w, m=min(w,n-start): f=-row*v; l=(i-start-(m-1)/2)*h. These are pre-anchor coordinates; here/target shifts and path fallback below can change final positions.

shapes.geometry: Start at (0,0). Let h=max(1.5,0.6*gap). Rings r=1,2,... have capacity6*r; take=min(capacity,remaining). For k=0..take-1, a=2*pi*k/take+(r odd?0:pi/capacity), slot=(r*h*cos(a),r*h*sin(a)). No CEN step. Ring radial increments are1.5/2.4/4.8 yards for tight/normal/wide; slot0 is centre, not the front despite the broad header comment.

For n=1: (max(min_radius,4),0). Otherwise R=clamp(n*gap/(2*pi),max(min_radius,3),35); slots at a=2*pi*k/n, (R*cos(a),R*sin(a)), starting ahead. No CEN. One ring, unlike active owner-follow concentric rings.

For n=1: (max(min_radius,4),0). Otherwise R=clamp(n*gap/pi,max(min_radius,4),35). Angles=-pi/2+pi*k/(n-1), including both side endpoints; stable-sort using abs(a)<abs(b)-0.0001, so nearest the front is assigned first, approximately symmetric ties retain original order. Slots=(R*cos(a),R*sin(a)). No CEN; only the forward semicircle. Formula uses n, not n-1, for radius.
width=ceil(sqrt(n)); cell=clamp(2.5*gap,6,12); ROW(n,width,cell,cell), then CEN. Tight produces6.25 yards, normal10, wide12. The code comment rounds tight to6; the formula gives6.25.
ROW(n,10,gap,gap), then CEN. Up to10 per row, up to4 rows for40 bots; the comment mentioning a second row does not impose a two-row maximum.
lanes=1 if n<=10, 2 if n<=20, otherwise3. ROW(n,lanes,gap,gap), then CEN. These cutoffs differ from owner-follow column geometry.

Tip(0,0); up to three head positions(-gap,(k-1)*gap), k=0..2; then rows r=2,3,... with shaft width2 for n<=12, 3 for n<=24, otherwise4, positions(-r*gap,(k-(width-1)/2)*0.9*gap). Stop at n and CEN all positions. Partial head/shaft rows keep the original k sequence before whole-shape centering.

Nine slots per V layer: layer=floor(i/9), k=i%9, back=1.6*gap*layer. k=0 ->(-back,0); otherwise j=floor((k+1)/2), sign=+1 for odd k else-1, slot=(-back-0.75*j*gap,sign*0.75*j*gap). CEN afterwards. Distinct from owner-follow eight-slot layers.

anchors.here: Default (also structured alias me): anchor is sender current XYZ, orientation is sender facing, min_radius=3. For non-ring shapes only, PushAhead raises minimum f to at least4 yards. Circle/Arc are exempt, so ring shapes go around the player. They are not all centred at the player after this shift.
anchors.target: Structured aliases target/my target: selected in-world Unit on same map, not sender, not a Player in sender group, at most100 horizontal yards from sender. Handler does not require target hostility or alive state. Anchor=current target XYZ; forward points FROM target TOWARD sender. min_radius=combat reach+2; non-ring shapes shifted to f>=that clearance. Circle/Arc use min_radius and no forward shift.
anchors.cursor: Structured aliases cursor/point/ping: saves latest request per sender for30000ms, then consumes next ground ping of any type or world marker. Pending entry is erased before expiry/point validation; now>deadline expires, equality is allowed. New cursor request replaces old. Bot selection and sender position/orientation are evaluated when the point arrives. Reject (x,y)==(0,0), or >100 horizontal yards from sender; if >1 yard away face sender->point (away from sender), else use sender facing. Anchor=point XYZ, min_radius=3, no PushAhead. CEN is still shape-specific (e.g. Arc is a forward semicircle, not centroid-centred).
anchors.transform: x=ax+cos(o)*f-sin(o)*l; y=ay+sin(o)*f+cos(o)*l; initial z=anchor z. FallbackSlotReachable snaps to ground at most6 vertical yards from anchor, requires normal path ending within2 horizontal yards, and if anchor path exists requires slot path length<=anchor path+1.5*offset+5. If full slot fails, try half offset; if that fails use anchor itself without another reachability check. Thus final slots may overlap and here/target clearance can be lost; queued movement is not arrival evidence.

selection_and_orders.selection: Requires sender session and group. Matches registered, controlled bots within that group, alive, same map, <=150 horizontal yards from anchor. Ownership-bound bots require matching owner; otherwise ControlsForGroupOrder resolves human controller. Select at most40 in group iteration order BEFORE sorting. Selectors OR together; none means all eligible bots. Names are case-insensitive. Role selectors tank(s), healer(s)/heal/heals, dps, melee (DPS only), ranged (DPS only); group1..8 maps to subgroup0..7; all/everyone/squad; the nine listed WoW classes singular/plural.
selection_and_orders.ordering: PlaceRankOf orders tanks, melee, ranged, healers, then ascending GUID. It assigns selected bots to geometry vector indices independently of manual slot pins. No ownership or slot reassignment of other bots.
selection_and_orders.effect: Queues a running MoveTo and manual Stay with kHoldPositionTtlMs=30*60*1000; pins each computed world return point, clears owner-follow, fallback, pull-back and owner-use. The source intention is return after fights, not proof of indefinite persistence or arrival. place follow/back/free dispatches ordinary Follow to chosen eligible bots. The response placed count is queued/intended action, not confirmed native movement.

parser_transport.text: ApplyPlaceOrder lowercases whitespace-delimited text: exact verb place, then required ONE shape token. First recognized gap token except close is gap; first here/target/cursor token is anchor; other tokens become who selectors. Order after shape is flexible. close as gap and me/point/ping/my target as anchors work at structured PlaceBots level but are not these text-parser aliases. Literal far apart is not one alias: far selects Spread and apart becomes a selector. Extra/repeated/unrecognized gap/anchor words also become selectors; not necessarily a syntax error. Missing/unknown shape rejects. Text place is intercepted before normal per-bot addressing, so an unqualified whisper place can act on all eligible controlled group bots, not just recipient.
parser_transport.addon: P.Fields sends chosen names with explicit shape/gap/anchor; initial circle/normal. UI refuses no selected names, limits sends to once per second, uses PLACE_REQ if ready, otherwise group-order text capped250 bytes (truncates names with warning). Server structured request takes first40 nonempty who fields, omitted who means all eligible (different from UI empty-selection refusal). Server answers a system line and PLACE_RESP; UI does not wait. Cursor uses a secure world-marker button or ground ping; no actual client or SWTOR slash transport was tested.

unknowns_and_limits: Source-only reading; actual pathfinding, packet/client delivery, cursor UI, arrival and persistence across restart are untested. No upstream code executed or target implementation performed.

RingRadius clamps to min_radius..35 for n>1, while the n=1 special case has no35-yard cap. There is no local guard here for target-derived min_radius>35; do not assert that unusual case has safe35-yard behavior.
Parser integer narrowing/overflow quirks are source caveats, not a proposed SWTOR contract. No game-native units, IDs, authority, control or movement rules are inferred.
